title: Ambition map + short asks (people ops personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick personal map of ambition + concise asks for upcoming 1:1s. Use as a live scratchpad — not polished. Keep bullets short so I can skim before manager catch-up.

Top-line (why this doc exists)
- Capture growth signals I want to amplify (skills, scope, influence).
- Short, prioritized asks I can actually get a yes/no on in a single 1:1.
- Evidence snippets to point to without fumbling.

3-6 month ambition (headline)
- Move from individual contributor people ops partner to owning one cross-functional initiative end-to-end (onboarding revamp or manager enablement).
- Build a repeatable onboarding metric (time-to-productivity) and run a pilot that improves 1 key metric by 10–15%.
- Increase visibility with PM/Eng leadership so I'm considered for manager-level workload in 12–18 months.

Success metrics I care about (draft)
- Pilot cohort NPS >= 7 (from baseline 5).
- New hire first-90-days survey completion rate >= 85% for pilot group.
- Time-to-first-merge (or product contribution) reduced by 20% for cohort.
- 3 cross-functional stakeholders (eng, product, onboarding ops) actively endorsing the program in retrospective.

Evidence vault (short snippets I can read aloud)
- 2026-02-21: ran onboarding interview with 4 new hires — common friction: environment setup and 'who to ask' unclear. Quote: 'took me a week to know who owned infra permissions'.
- Benchmarked 3 other companies' 1st-week checklists — have doc refs (linked_artifacts).
- Internal survey (Dec 2025) shows 42% of hires felt unclear about role expectations in first month.

Concrete asks (prioritized, one-liners to raise in 1:1)
1) Decision & bandwidth: "Can I own an onboarding pilot (Q2) with an OKR to reduce time-to-first-merge by 20%? I estimate 0.1 FTE from eng and product sponsorship."
2) Stakeholder intro: "Can you introduce me to Sasha (Head of Eng Onboarding) and Alex (PM for platform) and flag that this is a 2-sprint pilot?"
3) Headspace/time: "Can I carve 4 hours/week for 8 weeks (protected time) to run interviews, coordinate pilot?"

Priority is #1; if manager won't sign off, get #2 and we iterate scope.

Risks & mitigation (short)
- Risk: lack of eng time -> Mitigation: scope to smaller 'env setup' experiment first (reduces scope to infra playbook).
- Risk: low survey response -> Mitigation: embed survey in Slack onboarding check-in, offer small incentive.
- Risk: success metric depends on product cadence -> Mitigation: use proxy metric (time-to-first-successful-local-run) controllable by infra changes.

Career signal plan (what I want manager to notice)
- Leading cross-functional outcomes (not only tasks).
- Running a clean pilot end-to-end: problem diagnosis, hypothesis, experiment, measure, iterate.
- Presenting results with a clear ask for next step (scale or handoff).

Conversation prompts for 1:1 (quick lines)
- "I want to run a 8-week onboarding pilot — can I get your decision today?"
- "If not full approval, would an intro to Sasha/Alex help get buy-in?"
- "What would you want to see at mid-pilot to feel comfortable scaling?"
- "Can you help unblock X (budget / eng time) — who on leadership needs to sign?"

Feedback I need (from manager)
- Is this initiative the right signal for my career path? (scale vs IC specialization)
- Do you see any blind spots in the metric selection?
- What type of stakeholder endorsements would you count as endorsement for promotion readiness?

Mini experiments I can run before full pilot
- 1-week 'env-setup sprint' with 3 new hires to iterate a checklist. (2 days prep, 3 interviews, 2 days synth)
- Quick shadow of new-hire onboarding session with product onboarding lead (book this).
- Short A/B test of onboarding checklist delivery (Slack DM vs email) — measure open/completion.

Immediate TODO (next 7 days)
- Draft one-pager (1-pager) for pilot: problem, hypothesis, KPIs, stakeholders, ask (due Thu).
- DM Sasha & Alex for 10-min intro and seed the idea (today).
- Pull Dec 2025 survey raw responses + top 3 verbatim quotes for 1:1 (tomorrow).
- Block 4 hours on calendar for pilot work (tentative) and mark as "focus" on my calendar.

Notes-to-self (random, informal)
- Keep ask narrow. Managers hate vague asks. Give them a binary yes/no + small follow-ups.
- Practice the opener: "I need a decision on sponsorship and 0.1 FTE from eng — yes/no?"
- Do not over-qualify in the 1:1; bring the one-pager as print or a single slide.

Open questions / unknowns
- How much cross-team budget is reasonable for a pilot? (est. $2–4k for incentives + infra time?)
- Who signs off on new-hire survey distribution cadence?
- Are there existing dashboards I can reuse for time-to-productivity? (maybe analytics infra owns it)
__notes: scratchpad: rough, iterative. Delete or version before sharing externally.
